sourcedFrom: Ruger P-Series P89, P90, P94 & P944 Manual Safety Model Instruction Manual — V & KV (MS) 3/06 C R10 (2006)
cleanIntro: Ruger publishes separate P89 books for the manual-safety, decocker and double-action-only pistols, and this is the MANUAL SAFETY one. Every step below carries its words and the page they are printed on.

steps.title: Check you are on the right P89 book
steps.action: Before anything else, confirm your pistol has a manual safety lever on each side of the slide. This manual is for the P89 manual-safety pistols (KP89 and the KP89X Convertible included) and does not cover the decocker or the "double action only" pistols.
steps.prose: Ruger prints that exclusion on the cover. The three P89 variants differ in exactly the control you use in the very next step — an owner of a decocker following a safety-lever instruction is being told to move something the gun does not have.
steps.quote: RUGER® P-SERIES P89, P90TM P94TM & P944 MANUAL SAFETY MODEL PISTOLS* *DO NOT USE THIS MANUAL FOR DECOCKER MODEL PISTOLS OR “DOUBLE ACTION ONLY” PISTOLS
steps.cite: Ruger P-Series P89, P90, P94 & P944 Manual Safety Model Instruction Manual — V & KV (MS) 3/06 C R10 — Cover, p.1

steps.title: Safety on, magazine out
steps.action: Keep the pistol pointed in a safe direction, place either safety lever fully down in the "safe" position so the white dot and the letter "S" are exposed, then press forward on either magazine latch and withdraw the magazine.
steps.prose: The safety levers and the magazine latch are both ambidextrous, so either side does the job. The white dot and the "S" are how you confirm the safety is on rather than assuming it.
steps.quote: Keep pistol pointed in a safe direction and place either safety lever in the “safe” position (lever fully down, white dot and the letter “S” exposed). Press forward on either magazine latch and withdraw magazine from butt of pistol.
steps.cite: Ruger P-Series P89, P90, P94 & P944 Manual Safety Model Instruction Manual — V & KV (MS) 3/06 C R10 — To Disassemble, step 1, p.21
steps.warn: Always unload a firearm before cleaning, lubrication, disassembly or assembly.

steps.title: Lock the slide open and look
steps.action: Pull the slide to the rear and lock it open by pressing upward on the rear end of the slide stop, then confirm with your eyes that the chamber is empty.
steps.prose: Magazine out and chamber empty are two separate facts. Ruger warns elsewhere in the book that the pistol fires with the magazine out, which is why the chamber check is repeated here.
steps.quote: Pull slide to rear and lock in open position by pressing upward on rear end of slide stop. Again, be sure chamber is empty!
steps.cite: Ruger P-Series P89, P90, P94 & P944 Manual Safety Model Instruction Manual — V & KV (MS) 3/06 C R10 — To Disassemble, step 2, p.21

steps.title: Push the ejector down and forward
steps.action: Keep upward pressure on the slide stop, reach a finger through the top of the slide, and push the ejector downward and forward until it locks in its lower position.
steps.prose: This is the step people miss and then force. Until the ejector is latched down the slide cannot run forward, and no amount of pulling will change that.
steps.caution: Open slide is under strong spring tension and could injure fingers if allowed to slam shut.
steps.quote: until it locks in its lower position. This will permit forward movement of slide. Further disassembly is impossible unless this is done.
steps.cite: Ruger P-Series P89, P90, P94 & P944 Manual Safety Model Instruction Manual — V & KV (MS) 3/06 C R10 — To Disassemble, step 3, p.22

steps.title: Pin to the notch, slide stop out to the left
steps.action: Fingers out of the ejection port and a tight grip on the slide: press down on the slide stop and let the slide move slowly forward until the slide stop spring retainer pin lines up with the front edge of the slide stop notch. Press in on the right-hand end of the slide stop and pull it out to the left until it locks in its withdrawn position — do not pull it all the way out.
steps.prose: On the P89 the slide stop stays in the frame: it pulls out to a locked, withdrawn position and stops there. Trying to pull it free is the mistake this step invites, and the book tells you not to.
steps.quote: Now press down on slide stop and allow slide to move slowly forward until the slide stop spring retainer pin is aligned with the front edge of the slide stop notch. Press in on right-hand end of slide stop and pull slide stop out of frame to the left until it locks in its withdrawn position. (See Figure 5A, above.) Do not attempt to pull it completely out of the frame.
steps.cite: Ruger P-Series P89, P90, P94 & P944 Manual Safety Model Instruction Manual — V & KV (MS) 3/06 C R10 — To Disassemble, step 4, p.22

steps.title: Slide assembly off the front
steps.action: Push the slide forward and take the entire slide assembly off the front of the frame.
steps.prose: Straight off the front. With the slide stop withdrawn nothing is left holding the two halves together.
steps.quote: Push slide forward and remove entire slide assembly to the front.
steps.cite: Ruger P-Series P89, P90, P94 & P944 Manual Safety Model Instruction Manual — V & KV (MS) 3/06 C R10 — To Disassemble, step 5, p.22

steps.title: Guide rod and recoil spring out
steps.action: Hold the slide upside down, lift the rear end of the guide rod to unseat it from the barrel lug, then withdraw the spring and guide rod to the rear of the slide.
steps.prose: Lift the rear first — the rod seats against the barrel lug, so drawing it straight back while it is still seated just binds it. Keep a thumb on it: the spring is compressed.
steps.quote: With slide held upside down, lift rear end of guide rod to disengage it from its seat against the barrel lug. Withdraw spring and guide rod to the rear of the slide. CAUTION: Spring is under tension!
steps.cite: Ruger P-Series P89, P90, P94 & P944 Manual Safety Model Instruction Manual — V & KV (MS) 3/06 C R10 — To Disassemble, step 6, p.22

steps.title: Barrel out
steps.action: Pull the barrel slightly upward out of the slide and withdraw it to the rear.
steps.prose: Up a little, then back. The barrel has to clear its locking recess in the slide before it will travel.
steps.quote: Pull barrel upward out of slide slightly and withdraw to the rear.
steps.cite: Ruger P-Series P89, P90, P94 & P944 Manual Safety Model Instruction Manual — V & KV (MS) 3/06 C R10 — To Disassemble, step 7, p.22

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel, guide rod and recoil spring, and magazine — that is the whole strip Ruger documents for the P89.
steps.prose: This is as far as the book goes, and it is far enough to clean the pistol properly. Everything past it is factory work.
steps.quote: This completes normal fieldstripping for routine cleaning and lubrication purposes. Further disassembly of slide or frame components is not recommended and should only be undertaken by the factory.
steps.cite: Ruger P-Series P89, P90, P94 & P944 Manual Safety Model Instruction Manual — V & KV (MS) 3/06 C R10 — To Disassemble, step 8, p.23

deepAbsentReason: Ruger ends this book’s disassembly at step 8 on p.23: "Further disassembly of slide or frame components is not recommended and should only be undertaken by the factory." It documents nothing past the field strip, so this listing has no deep clean. That is the manual’s answer, not a gap in ours.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Run a solvent-wetted patch through the bore several times with a cleaning rod
Attach a solvent-wetted bristle brush and run it back and forth the full length of the bore as many times as needed to clear grease and dirt from bore and chamber
Clean the bore with dry patches and examine it — Ruger warns bore fouling costs accuracy and grease in the chamber interferes with feeding from the magazine

cleaning.name: ALL COMPONENTS OF THE MECHANISM
tasks: Remove powder residue from every component with powder solvent on a clean patch or bristle brush
Run a dry patch through the bore, then follow it with a very lightly oiled one
Wipe all surfaces clean with cloth, then wipe them with a patch or cloth that is very lightly oiled

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Check the follower moves freely and has enough tension to lift each cartridge to the feeding position
Check the magazine lips are clean and free of cracks, dents or nicks
After soaking a dirty magazine, shake it vigorously with the loading opening away from you — Ruger warns solvent left inside can kill or weaken primers
Do not use a magazine whose follower tension cleaning does not restore — Ruger says get a new one

cleaning.name: BEFORE YOU SHOOT IT AGAIN
tasks: Remove all oil and grease from the bore before firing
Keep the oil light — Ruger warns excess oil attracts dust and can congeal in cold weather

reassembly: Be certain the chamber and magazine are empty.
With the slide held upside down, replace the barrel and push it rearward into its locked position.

Replace the guide rod and recoil spring, the smaller-diameter end of the spring against the collar; the rear end of the guide rod seats against the barrel lug. The barrel link must stand vertical with its hole showing, or the pistol cannot be reassembled.

KP89X Convertible: the barrel and the recoil spring/guide rod go in as a matched pair — the 9mm barrel with the tapered rod and the spring that extends past it, the .30 Luger barrel with the captive spring on the untapered rod. Ruger cautions the wrong combination could cause malfunction or damage.
Be certain the ejector is locked in its lower (forward) position and the hammer is in its fired (uncocked) position.
Replace the slide onto the frame.
Pull the slide back until the disassembly notch is opposite the lug on the slide stop, then press the slide stop all the way through the frame to the right.
Allow the slide to move fully forward.
Replace the empty magazine through the butt — that is what returns the ejector to its working position. Ruger warns the pistol will not function normally unless the ejector is up (rearward).
fncheck: With the pistol and its magazine confirmed empty and the muzzle in a safe direction: the slide has moved fully forward, and the empty magazine is back in the frame — Ruger says that is what returns the ejector to its working position, and that the pistol will not function normally unless the ejector is up (rearward).
